articles.headline: The Gradient Is a Covariance
articles.blurb: Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.

articles.headline: Mo' turns, mo' problems
articles.blurb: Doing reinforcement learning for agent use-cases is conceptually not at all that complicated. For each problem, you set up a VM with a harness and a fresh model context, send the prompt, let the model make tool calls, score the whole thing at the end, and update the weights. Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

articles.headline: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing
articles.blurb: Google Quantum AI has demonstrated that 'magic state cultivation' works in practice on its Willow processor. Magic states help researchers create the operations they need for going beyond classical computing. Creating high-quality, error-corrected magic states is incredibly resource-heavy. This post details how Google Quantum AI created a magic state cultivation protocol that achieved a 40-fold reduction in errors. The breakthrough is a crucial step towards scaling up quantum computing to practical use.

articles.headline: How to Train Your Robot

Researchers are now working hard to gather enormous amounts of robot task training data in the hopes of seeing the same sort of trends with robotic capabilities.

A human is still required to decide what to build and check that the fix runs on real hardware, but AI takes away a lot of the slog. Reps get paid for meetings held with decision makers, and account executives don't prospect. Managers supervise just four or five reps each. Selling multiple products to each customer helps fund that staffing. It caps payment per thousand views at measured revenue per thousand views, favoring flat fees to keep viral upside. One creator went from roughly 10,000 views to 7 million. articles.headline: Put a name on it

Reading roughly 30 updates takes leadership 30 to 60 minutes, leaving four to six projects needing closer attention. The owner can book Wednesday office hours directly with leadership. articles.headline: Abstract Warfare: How TSMC Made Its Own Market
articles.blurb: TSMC made it possible to start a chip company without building a factory or depending on a manufacturer that sold competing chips. It manufactured for other designers and committed not to compete with them. A factory's huge upfront cost became something a designer could pay for as its business grew. TSMC initially survived on work existing chipmakers didn't want, while its future customers were still forming. After initially working on Parkinson's, the company shifted to essential tremor, citing more patients and less drug-development activity. Its clearance covers adults with essential tremor. articles.headline: Inside Hyperdrive: How We Solved a Rare MySQL Caching Bug

articles.blurb: Monzo raised $500M at a $4.5B valuation in late 2021, near the peak of fintech VC funding. Its last employee share sale last year nudged that to $5.9B. That's a 31% gain in three years, while annual revenue grew from £154M to the current £1.7B. Over the same period, competitor Revolut went from $33B in 2021 to $115B in a secondary sale this July, a 3.5x increase. That prices Revolut at roughly 19x its 2025 revenues vs. Monzo's 3x revenues.
